mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets the model construct two distinct audit entries describing the same (application, prev_status, new_status) transition, which is exactly the append-only/duplicate violation the assertion forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.application = ae2.application and ae1.prevStatus = ae2.prevStatus and ae1.newStatus = ae2.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows the auto-assignment to produce an application whose assigned officer is the same user as the applicant, violating FR-011.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfAssignmentViolation { some a: LoanApplication | some a.assignedOfficer and a.assignedOfficer = a.applicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a successful PATCH where the caller is the application's applicant (self-decision) or not its assigned officer — both forbidden by FR-012/FR-013/FR-024.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfDecisionViolation { some op: Operation | op.response = Ok and op.kind = PatchStatus and some op.target and op.caller = op.target.applicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets an unauthorized GET on an existing application return Ok instead of the byte-equivalent NotFound, leaking the application's existence to an outsider.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeakageViolation { some op: Operation | op.kind = GetApplication and op.authenticated = True and some op.target and op.response = Ok and not legitimateApplicationRead[op] }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets an unauthenticated request succeed with response Ok, bypassing the OAuth bearer requirement that FR-001 makes mandatory before any business logic.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBypass { some op: Operation | op.authenticated = False and op.response = Ok and op.kind = GetApplication }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets the model produce an audit entry for a failed (non-Ok) operation, violating the atomic-commit guarantee of FR-017 and the validation-before-mutation pattern.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditForFailedOp { some op: Operation | op.response != Ok and some op.resultingAudit }
